comment: This class seemed to me a bit outdated and his lectures were tedious. We barely discussed the readings but they popped up on the exams. Assignments were easy, but midterm was cruel. The final group project ended up being much more work than expected (5-7 mins is long for a short film). By no means an easy class but was interesting at times.

Great guy, bad prof. It's a lecture-heavy film class, meaning each class is spent listening to Dr. Riehl ramble about his favorite artists and movies. Students used it as a blow-off, browsing on their laptops almost all of every class. Little to no effort is made to engage the class past a few surface-level discussion questions at start of class.
He is nice and knowledgeable about the subject. Two tests, a project, and some homework so not too difficult. Class could be boring if you don't enjoy the subject.

A great conductor - accompanied by Dr. Bennett, Schola is a strong choir. Would recommend joining if you enjoying singing more traditional music and the beautiful sounds of a talented choir. You need some prior singing experience but no real training is required beyond understanding basic music theory.

By far, Dr. Riehl is the best choral director I have ever had. He makes Schola Cantorum super fun. Show up to all rehearsals and concerts and you will get an A. His reputation at UR and in the music dept is unmatched. His humor and wit coupled with great musical skills make SC enjoyable regardless of whether you have had formal vocal training.

Dr. Riehl is my favorite professor at UR. He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about music and film studies & does a great job breaking it down for music majors and non-majors. Though he assigns a fair bit of academic reading in addition to 12 films (1 weekly), he guides you to draw your own conclusions and observations. Awesome prof!

Took this class for arts gen ed, definitley the right choice. I don't know much about music or film and did well. Pay attention to what he says about the different films in class and you'll be golden on the exams. Final group film project was super fun, and there are four short, casual writing assignments throughout the semester on select films.

Hearing in Cinema: interesting topic. Sometimes he talked way above my basic knowledge of music making it difficult to follow his lectures. He's always willing to help & I suggest talking to him about  your papers- it's worth it! A great choice fys with little reading (at least none you HAVE to do). Put the time in with paper and you will be fine

Schola Cantorum.....awesome group if you're interested in a music major or even if you want to continue singing from high school.  Dr. Riehl is the best director I've ever had; he loves what he does and knows music inside and out. Attend rehearsals and concerts and you'll get an A.  Highly recommended!
